CARDINO VS. DOMINADOR G. JALOSLOS, JR." The dispositive portion of the aforesaid COMELEC writ of Execution reads: 'NOW, THEREFORE, you are hereby DIRECTED to immediately implement this Writ of Execution by serving a copy hereof together with certified true copy of the Resolutions of the First Division, and of the En Banc, of this Commission, dated May IO, 2010 and August 11, 2011, respectively, upon Vice Mayor Patri Bajamunde-Chan ordering him to cease and desist from performing the functions as Acting Mayor of Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte, and immediately make a return of the service within five (5) days therefrom. " As stated in your letter the following are the antecedent facts: Dominador G. Jalosjos (Jalosjos, for brevity) and Agapito J. Cardino (Cardino, for brevity) were the candidates for the position of Mayor in Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte in the 2010 National and Local Elections; On 06 December 2009, Cardino filed before the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) a petition under Section 78 of Batas Pambansa Blg. 8811 seeking to deny due course and to cancel the certificate of candidacy of Jalosjos entitled, "Agapito J. Cardino vs. Dominador G. Jalosjos, Jr." (SPA No. 09-076 [DC]); On IO May 2010, the COMELEC First Division promulgated a Resolution in the above-entitled case, the dispositive portion of which reads: "WHEREFORE, premises considered, the instant Petition is hereby Granted. Accordingly, the Certificate of Candidacy of respondent Dominador G Jalosjos,Jr. is hereby cancelled. " Thereafter, Jalosjos filed a Motion for Reconsideration of the above Resolution; On 11 August 2010, the COMELEC En Banc issued a Resolution denying the Motion for Reconsideration filed by Jalosjos. The dispositive portion of the aforesaid COMELEC En Banc Resolution reads: "WHEREFORE, in of the foregoing, the Motion for Reconsideration is denied for utter lack of' merit. Respondent [Jalosjos] is hereby OUSTED from office and ordered to CEASE and DESIST from occupying and discharging the functions of the Office of the Mayor of Dapitan City, Zamboanga. Let the provisions of the Local Government Code on succession apply. " On 25 August 2010, Jalosjos filed a petition before the Supreme Court (Jalosjos petition, for brevity) appealing the afore-quoted COMELEC En Banc Resolution, and was docketed as G.R. No 193237; Also known as the "Omnibus Election Code".

Page 3 of 7 On 17 September 2010, Cardino likewise filed a petition before the Supreme Court (Cardino petition, for brevity) questioning the aforesaid COMELEC En Banc Resolution, particularly on the addition in the dispositive portion of the application of the provisions of succession under Republic Act No. 71602. The Cardino Petition was entitled "Agapito J. Cardino vs. Dominador Jalosjos" and docketed as G.R. No. 193536; On 22 February 2011, the Supreme Court issued a Resolution dismissing G.R. No. 193237 (Jalosjos' petition), the dispositive portion of which reads: " WHEREFORE, the foregoing premises considered, the Petition for Certiorari is DISMISSED. The assailed Resolution dated May 10, 2010 and Resolution dated August I I, 2010 of the Commission on Elections in SPA Case No. 09-076 (DC) are hereby AFFIRMED': On 17 March 2011, Cardino filed a Manifestation before the Supreme Court praying that the above Resolution be taken judicial notice in relation to his petition; On 29 March 2011, the Supreme Court resolved to consolidate G.R. No. 193536 with G.R. No. 193237; On 01 June 2012, Jalosjos filed a Manifestation stating that "he has resigned from the position of Mayor of the City of Dapitan effective 30 April 2012" which resignation was accepted by the Provincial Governor of Zamboanga del Norte, Atty. Rolando E. Yebes. Jalosjos' resignation was for the purpose of acquiring a residence at Zamboanga del Sur to comply with the residency requirement vis-å-vis the provisions of the Omnibus Election Code in preparation of his candidacy as Provincial Governor of Zamboanga del Sur in May 2013 National and Local Elections; On 09 October 2012, the Supreme Court issued a Resolution on the consolidated cases of G.R. No. 193536 and G.R. No. 193237, the dispositive portion of which reads: "WHEREFORE, the Motion for Reconsideration in G.R. No. 193237 is DENIED, and the Petition in G.R. No. 19353bisGRANTED. The Resolutions dated IOMay 2010 and 11 August 2010 of the COMELEC First Division and the COMELEC En Banc, respectively, in SPA No. 09-07b (DC), are AFFIRMED with the MODIFICATION that Agapito J. Cardino ran unopposed in May 2010 elections and thus received the 2 Also known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 ".

Cardino; xxv • On 15 January 2012, the COMELEC received a Manifestation ( To The "Urgent Motion") filed by Cardino attaching therewith a certified true copy of the Entry of Judgment dated November 21, 2012 issued by the Supreme Court in G.R. Nos. 193237 and 193536;

Page 5 of 7 • On 16 January 2013, the COMELEC received a copy of the Supreme Court Resolution dated December II, 2012, granting the Urgent Motion for Entry of Judgment filed by the counsel of Cardino; • On 17 January 2013, the COMELEC En Banc issued a writ of Execution directing the Honorable Secretary of this Department, among others, to cause the implementation of the COMELEC En Banc Resolution, the dispositive portion of which reads: "NOW THEREFORE, you are hereby DIRECTED to immediately implement this Writ of Execution by serving a copy hereof together with certified true copy of the Resolutions of the First Division, and of the En Banc, of' this Commission, dated May 10, 2010 and August 11, 2011, respectively, upon Vice Mayor Patri Bajamunde- Chan ordering him to cease and desist from performing the functions as Acting Mayor of Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte, and immediately make a return of the service within five (5) days therefrom. " On 23 January 2013, Hon. Patri Bajamunde Chan (Vice-Mayor Chan, for brevity), the duly elected Vice Mayor of Dapitan City filed a Petition for Prohibition and Certiorari with Temporary Restraining Order and/or Writ of Preliminary Injunction, assailing the Writ of Execution issued by the COMELEC. Vice-Mayor Chan assumed the office of the Mayor of Dapitan City due to the resignation of former Mayor Jalosjos; • On 24 January 2013, the Special City Board of Canvassers of the COMELEC proclaimed Cardino as the duly elected Mayor of Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte, and accordingly the latter took his oath of office before that Board; • On 24 January 2013, this Department received the above-mentioned COMELEC Writ of Execution; Hence, you are now requesting a legal opinion on the following queries; to wit: 1. Whether or not Ms. Patri B. Chan who assumed as Mayor due to the resignation of former Mayor Dominador Jalosjos, Jr. is duty bound to return to her former position as Vice-Mayor pursuant to the Writ of Execution issued by the COMELEC En Banc regarding the implementation of the afore-quoted COMELEC En Banc Resolution; 2. If so, can her acts during her incumbency as a full-pledged Mayor be considered legitimate and valid acts pursuant to the afore-quoted Comelec En Banc Resolution?

Page 6 of 7 3. What is the status of the 1st Ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod member who assumed as Vice Mayor? Is he duty bound to return to his former position as 1st Ranking Sangguniang Panglungsod member? 4. If so, can his acts during his incumbency as Vice Mayor be also considered legitimate and valid? 5. What is the status of the Sangguniang Panlungsod Member who was appointed to fill-up the vacancy caused by the 1st Ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod who assumed as Vice Mayor? We shall address your above-enumerated queries in one discussion since they are related. As stated in the above recital of facts, Jolosjos resigned as Mayor of Dapitan City effective 30 April 2012. Since voluntary resignation is one of the grounds enumerated in the second to the last paragraph3 of Section 44 of Republic Act No. 7160 causing permanent vacancy in a local elective office, the rule on succession set forth in the first paragraph4 of the same provision of Republic Act No. 7160 shall be applied by operation of law, meaning there is no more need for the doing of an operative act. Hence, when Jalojos resigned as Mayor Of Dapitan City, Vice-Mayor Chan must assume the aforesaid position. The same is true in the case of the first-ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod member who shall assume as Vice-Mayor. Subsequent vacancies in the said office shall be filled automatically by the other sanggunian members according to their ranking. Let it be noted however that when Jolosjos resigned as Mayor of Dapitan City effective 30 April 2012 (the incident which gave rise to the application of the rule on succession), the two (2) special civil actions for certiorari5 questioning the resolution of the COMELEC in SPA No. 09-076 (DC) are yet to be decided by the Supreme Court. Hence, while it is true that voluntary resignation is one of the grounds of permanent vacancy in a local elective office which necessarily paved the way for the application of the Section 44, RA No. 7160 For purposes of this Chapter, a permanent vacancy arises when an elective local official fills a higher vacant office, reiüses to assume office, fails to qualify, dies, is removed from office, or is otherwise permanently incapacitated to discharge the functions of his office." No. , 193237 seeking to annul the 10 May 2010 Resolution of the COMELEC First Division and the 11 August 2010 Resolution Of the COMELEC En Banc, which both ordered the cancellation of his certificate of candidacy on the ground of false material representation. While the second was filed by Cardino in G.R. No. 193536 challenging the 1 1 August 2010 Resolution of the COMELEC En Banc, which applied the rule on succession under the Local Government Code in filling the vacancy in the Office of the Mayor of Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte created by the cancellation of Jalosjos' certificate of candidacy.

Page 7 of 7 rule on succession in the case at hand, such application of rule on succession shall always be subject to the outcome of the pending cases before the Supreme Court. Accordingly, when the Supreme Court rendered a Decision on 09 October 2012 declaring that Cardino ran unopposed in the May 2010 elections and thus received the highest number of votes for Mayor of Dapitan City, and the COMELEC En Banc issued a Writ of Execution on 17 January 2013 directing the Secretary of this Department, among others, to cause its implementation and accordingly order Vice-Mayor Chan to cease and desist from performing the functions as Mayor of Dapitan City, Vice-Mayor Chan is therefore duty bound to return to her position as Vice —Mayor of Dapitan City to which she was elected in the 2010 elections. The same is true with regard to Lhe case of the 1st ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Member, Atty. Ruben Cad, who assumed as Vice-Mayor. Atty. Cad is also duty bound to return his position as the 1st Ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Member, the position where he was elected in the 2010 elections. As to the appointed Sangguniang Panlungsod member who filled-up the vacancy caused by the 1st ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Member who assumed as Vice —Mayor of Dapitan City, as stated, Vice-Mayor Chan and Atty. Cad should slide down to their respective former positions as Vice-Mayor and 1st Ranking Sangguniang Panlungsod Member respectively. As such, there will no longer be any vacancy in the Sangguniang Panlungsod. The person thus appointed to fill-up the vacancy caused by Atty. Cad in the Sangguniang Panlungsod must also vacate pursuant to the Supreme Court ruling. As to the issue on the legitimacy or validity of the acts clone by Vice-Mayor Chan and Atty. Cad during their incumbencies as full-pledged Mayor and Vice-Mayor, respectively, we are of the view that all their acts in the performance of their respective duties and functions during their tenures as Mayor and Vice-Mayor, respectively, of Dapitan City were legitimate and valid. Vice-Mayor Chan and Atty. Cad at the very least may be considered as de facto officers6. Let it be noted that the assumption of Vice Mayor Chan and Atty. Cad as Mayor and Vice-Mayor, respectively, of Dapitan City happened before the Supreme Court issued the aforementioned Decision on 09 October 2012. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. LS:94/17/11 Very truly yours, JESUS Di OQ lv tor 11 6 A defdcto officer is defined by the Supreme Court in the case of Torres vs. Ribo (81 Phil 44) as One who has the reputation of being the officer that he assumes to be, and yet is not a good officer in point of law. He must have acted as Officer for such length of time, under color of title and under such circumstances Of reputation or acquiescence by the public and public authorities, as to afford a presumption of election or appointment, and induce people, without injury and relying on the supposition that he is the officer he assumes to be, to submit to or invoke his action. The acts of a de facto officer may be given validity in the eye of the law (Codilla, et al. vs. Martinez, G.R. No. L- 14569. 23 November 1960). The acts Of the de facto officer are just as valid for all purposes as those of a de jure officer, insofar as the public or third persons who are interested therein are concerned (Funa vs. Agra, G.R. No. 191644, 19 February 2013) . On the other hand, a dejure officer is a person who has Che lawlill right to the office in all respects, but has either been ousted from it, or who has never actually taken possession Of it.
